explanation: Apart from one rainforest species also found in Africa and southern Asia, cacti come from the Americas. Africa's cactus lookalikes are mostly euphorbias, which evolved a similar shape separately.

claims.text: Cacti are native to the Americas.
Apart from Rhipsalis baccifera, no cactus is native to Africa, the Middle East or Australia; cacti growing wild there were introduced by people.
One cactus species, Rhipsalis baccifera, is native to Africa and southern Asia as well as the Americas.
Many cactus-like succulents of Africa are euphorbias, which evolved a similar form independently.

evidence.restatement: Cacti are native to the Americas.
The only cactus with a natural range outside the Americas is Rhipsalis baccifera; other wild cacti in Africa, the Middle East and Australia were introduced by people.
Rhipsalis baccifera grows naturally in tropical Africa, Madagascar and Sri Lanka as well as in the Americas.
Cactus-like succulents in Africa are largely euphorbias, which evolved a similar shape independently.

issues.note: One species, Rhipsalis baccifera, is native to Africa, so 'Africa' is not wrong for every cactus. The explanation discloses it, and 'they' in the stem means cacti as a family, so it is not a second answer. 'Almost all' in the stem would make it airtight.
